Independent homogeneous elimination, incidence argument, rank decomposition and Segre-class computation
correctness.rationale: For invertible A and B the first two bilinear equations globally give y and x by their kernel lines over P1_z. Substituting in the third gives the homogeneous binary quadratic P; its derivative vanishes at a repeated zero in characteristic two exactly when its middle coefficient Q is zero, including the identically zero case. Expansion gives tr(AJB^TJCJ). Its coefficient of c0 is the irreducible 2×2 determinant a2b3+a3b2, which does not divide the coefficient of c1, so the linear polynomial in C is primitive and irreducible. The universal nontransverse incidence is irreducible: at a fixed base point three evaluations are independent and the six active derivatives freely specifiable; their sparse determinant is the irreducible binomial of disjoint triple products. This fibre description is locally trivial over the three P1s. The incidence image is closed by projectivity and meets the invertible open at F1=y+z, F2=x+z, F3=xy. Its intersection there agrees with V(Q), so the global reduced image equals V(Q). In the gradient, the trace pairing identifies sets of four derivatives with UV, VW and WU. If a matrix is invertible the other two vanish. Otherwise every rank is at most one and each intermediate line can be chosen between the incoming image and outgoing kernel. These choices yield the rank-three projective bundle of the record; generically the lines are recovered by the images of nonzero matrices, giving a rational inverse and dimension five. In its Segre class coefficient, the six ordered (2,1,0) exponent patterns contribute two each, the (1,1,1) pattern contributes two, and pure cubes vanish. Thus the degree is fourteen. Restricting to one nonzero block leaves its rank-one determinant quadric; the coordinate spaces are disjoint. The integral quadratic discriminant specializes to Q²; its primitivity can also be seen from the coefficient 1 on a2²b3²c0² in p1²−4p0p2.
residual_risks: This verifies the reduced singular locus, not the structure of the Jacobian scheme. The finite F2 check in the frozen package is corroboration, not a proof over the algebraic closure.

evidence: Circular-complex rank loci are irreducible orbit closures and components correspond to maximal ranks in the stated characteristic-zero theory. The inequalities r_i+r_(i+1)≤2 yield exactly (1,1,1) and the three placements of (2,0,0). The balanced Nash formula recovers the characteristic-zero discriminant degree, not the reduced small-characteristic object.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The formal component patterns are covered by a broader rank framework. The theorem targeted here also identifies the actual global reduced discriminant in characteristic two and computes its first singular locus; neither broader statement has that conclusion.

evidence: The primitive quadratic discriminant reduces formally to the square of its middle coefficient. The earlier degree, coordinate strata and factorized family describe subvarieties, not all nontransverse systems in characteristic two, nor all singular points of the cubic obtained after reduction.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The reduced and specialized Jacobian operations cannot be interchanged: differentiating the specialized square would give zero everywhere. A global incidence argument and the gradient of the reduced cubic are needed to establish that precisely these four loci exhaust its first reduced singular locus. The degree and rank-one quadrics are elementary once those families are identified, not independent novelty claims.

evidence: In the nonzero rank-one part, write A=m n^T, B=l n'^T, C=l' m'^T. The three product equations force n proportional to n', l to l', and m to m', since the determinant pairing in dimension two vanishes exactly on proportional vectors. This is the shared-factor family F1=M(y)N(z), F2=L(x)N(z), F3=L(x)M(y) in the prior concurrent-line description, not a mere dimensional coincidence.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The family of nonzero shared factors and its projective closure have the same parameterization in both characteristics, with an intrinsic bundle computation of degree. Its identification as a component of the first reduced singular locus of the characteristic-two Nash cubic does not follow from the description of deeper strata of the complex sextic.

evidence: Table 1 gives Δ3l dimension 5, one component and degree 14; Proposition 3.17 gives the three coordinate 3-planes Δscr. Table 3 puts Δ3l in the fourth iterated singular locus and Δscr in the third of the characteristic-zero sextic, whose first reduced singular locus has dimension 8 and seven components. originality.rationale: Credit the global identification and exhaustion of the first reduced singular locus of the characteristic-two Nash discriminant, including how the components meet there. The older literature already gives the primitive sextic, the same factorized degree-fourteen family in characteristic zero, and the same three coordinate strata there. Neither the number fourteen for that family nor the existence of those coordinate loci deserves separate originality credit. The first reduced singular locus in characteristic two is a distinct assertion, not the characteristic-zero singular-locus table carried over by substitution.
residual_risks: An unindexed trace-cubic or circular-complex treatment could overlap additional geometry. The strongest verified overlap is the already-reported degree of the same factorized family over characteristic zero, not historical priority for the entire characteristic-two first singular-locus statement.

value.rationale: This identifies what replaces the first singular stratification of a well-studied discriminant after bad-characteristic reduction. The collapse of the defining sextic to a square would make a specialized sextic gradient uninformative; the reduced cubic has a substantially different first singular locus, with the surviving strata and their incidences specified. This gives geometric information beyond the elementary square factorization or the already recorded degree of one shared stratum.
residual_risks: Not a method for general formats and not a statement about Jacobian scheme multiplicities.
